newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran condemns attack on Tajikistan's president.
newsitem.headline: Iran condemns attack on Tajikistan's president.

text.p: Iran condemned an assassination attempt on the president of Tajikistan and urged the government and the republic's armed Islamic opposition to work for national reconciliation, the state news agency IRNA reported on Thursday.
Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov was wounded on Wednesday by a grenade thrown as he got out of a car during a visit to the northern town of Khudjand.
Two people were killed and 60 injured. Rakhmonov was hit in the legs, but a presidential spokesman said his health was not endangered.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Mohammad Mohammadi said Iran condemned the attack but hoped the "belligerent Tajik sides will do all in their power to safeguard the achievements of the peace talks until national reconciliation is fully in place."
Iran has hosted peace talks between Tajikistan's government and the Islamic opposition to end the former Soviet republic's four-year civil war that has killed tens of thousands of people.
The latest talks, sponsored by the United Nations, were suspended in May, but were due to resume in Tehran on May 16.
